subject.title: Session transcript doomloop: crash-restart cycle inflates transcript until gateway OOMs

question: What default recovery policy should OpenClaw apply when an active session transcript is too large or repeatedly poisons gateway startup?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the fix must choose between preserving data, truncating or rotating history, skipping a bad session, marking it degraded, and adding media dedupe; automation should not choose that user-data policy alone.

options.title: Default Safe Quarantine
options.body: Before whole-file repair/open, detect oversized or repeatedly failing active transcripts, move them out of the hot path, expose a clear recovery/doctor path, and preserve data for manual inspection.

options.title: Default Tail Rotation
options.body: Automatically compact or rotate oversized active transcripts into a bounded successor before the next run, accepting a more invasive rewrite path.

options.title: Partial Marker Cap Only
options.body: Land only the bootstrap-marker circuit breaker and leave transcript-size and bad-session recovery to later work, accepting that crash loops can still recur from other oversized transcript causes.

recommendation.title: Default Safe Quarantine
recommendation.body: Before whole-file repair/open, detect oversized or repeatedly failing active transcripts, move them out of the hot path, expose a clear recovery/doctor path, and preserve data for manual inspection.

likelyOwner.reason: They have recent history across the active runner, bootstrap helper, and session repair paths implicated by the policy choice.
